title: Fortune Teller
story: You crack open a fortune cookie and read: 'An exciting opportunity awaits you.' Wouldn't it be cool to build your own digital fortune teller that gives a new prediction every time?
why: Combining random numbers with if/elif creates interactive programs that respond differently depending on chance.
analogy: A fortune teller is like a choose-your-own-adventure book — the random number picks which page (fortune) you land on.
try_it: Add two more fortunes by changing the range to 1-5 and adding more `elif` branches. Make them creative!
tips: Use `elif` to check additional conditions after the first `if` — you can chain as many as you need
The `else` branch is your safety net — it catches anything that didn't match earlier conditions
Make your fortunes fun and creative — this is your program, personalize it
common_mistakes: Using `else if` instead of `elif` — in XIOM, the keyword is `elif` (no space)
Forgetting to update the random range when adding more fortunes — if range is 1-3 but you have 5 fortunes, the last two never run
